title: Mission 14: The Handover
story: Two teammates joined the project: analyst 'aday' and the service account 'reportd'. Files created before they arrived all belong to YOU - and until ownership moves, nothing works for them. chown transfers the deed. Ownership changes need root: this is the mission where sudo earns its place in your toolbelt.

badge.name: The Handover: Deeds Transferred
badge.desc: Mastered chown by transferring files, groups and whole trees to their rightful owners.

tasks.brief: Read BRIEFING14.txt in your department directory. Transfer handover/analysis.txt to its new owner: user 'aday' (ownership changes need sudo - that is by design, not an obstacle).

checks.fail: analysis.txt is not owned by aday yet (sudo chown aday <file>).
analysis.txt content changed. A deed transfer moves the NAME on the door, nothing inside.

tasks.brief: handover/shared_notes.txt stays YOURS, but its GROUP must become 'analysts' so the whole team reads it. Change ONLY the group (chown has :group syntax, or the chgrp cousin).

checks.fail: shared_notes.txt's group is not analysts yet (chown :analysts, or chgrp).
The OWNER changed too. This order was group-only; the file stays yours.

tasks.brief: The nightly job file handover/nightly.dat goes fully to the service account: owner 'reportd' AND group 'analysts' in ONE command (owner:group syntax).

checks.fail: nightly.dat's owner is not reportd yet.
nightly.dat's group is not analysts (owner and group travel together with owner:group).

tasks.brief: Everything under handover/aday_workspace/ (files at every depth) becomes aday's - owner AND group 'analysts' - recursively in one command.

checks.fail: aday_workspace/ itself is not aday:analysts yet.
The nested drafts/plan.txt did not change hands - the transfer must be recursive.

tasks.brief: Prove the handover took: the service account must actually READ its file now. Run: sudo -u reportd cat handover/nightly.dat - and save that command's output to handover/proof.txt (as yourself).

checks.fail: proof.txt must be exactly what reportd sees when reading nightly.dat (run the cat AS reportd with sudo -u, redirect as yourself).
Even the briefing changed hands. Transfer exactly what the orders name - a recursive chown aimed too high grabs everything.
Your private notes were handed over too. Precision: the orders never named that file.

tasks.brief: BONUS: handover/template.txt must copy its ownership FROM another file rather than from names you type: make it match nightly.dat's owner and group using chown's --reference option.

checks.fail: template.txt must carry nightly.dat's POST-handover ownership (reportd:analysts). Finish the nightly.dat transfer first, then chown --reference copies it.
